_comment: This is the only file you need to edit from season to season. Everything else looks after itself.

eras._comment: Conferences arrived in season three. Everything before that is BCE.

divisional_weeks._comment: Weeks 10-14 are mostly in-conference. Each of those weeks also carries one inter-conference game between the two teams that finished in the same place in their conference last season - 5th v 5th first, working up to the two conference winners in the final week. Sleeper already schedules these; we only name them. Keys are last season's conference finishing position. Rename freely.

playoff_rounds._comment: Playoffs run in conference until the final. Keyed by week number.

side_competitions._comment: Champions, 7th and 10th are read from the Sleeper brackets, never typed here. 10th is always Loser of All Losers. The consolation bracket winner takes 7th and the 1.01; that trophy is renamed each year after the leading college prospect. Blank shows as 'Consolation bracket'. Champion GIFs and loser pictures go in assets/records via scripts/prepare_media.py.

manual_trades._comment: Trades Sleeper never recorded: deals done by hand on draft day, with the picks moved in the draft room and any player moved by the commissioner. Every other trade comes straight from Sleeper, so only add one here if it never went through as a Sleeper trade. List them in the order they happened; the date is UTC, with a time if it has to sort against other trades that day. Each side is what that manager received. A pick is 'season round original-owner' - '2025 3 Dave' is Dave's 2025 third - and shows as the player taken once the draft is done. Players go by name, or by Sleeper id if the name is not unique. If the Trade Centre shows a loose end, a trade is missing from here.

power_rankings._comment: Reproduces the Power Rankings tab of the Team Tracking workbook, week by week: score = (the last two weeks you played, plus this week's projected points, averaged) - your opponent's projected points. Week one has nothing behind it, so it is simply the difference between the two projections. The week's ranking is fixed at noon UK on the Wednesday before its games and never moves again; each one is kept in data/power_rankings.json. Nothing to edit here.

calendar._comment: The league year, as the old site's Calendar page had it. Every date is worked out - the free agency auction (third Monday in August), the roster deadline, the first waivers, kickoff, the playoff weeks, the trade deadline, the championship and the rookie draft all follow from Sleeper and the rules - so the only dates here are the two Sleeper cannot know. Add a year to pro_bowl or meeting and it appears on the page; leave it out and it does not. Dates are British: the NFL's Thursday night is our Friday morning, which is why a playing week reads Friday to Tuesday. The notes are yours to edit and show under the date they belong to.

pro_bowl: Standard JADL half PPR TEP scoring.
Lineup: 2 QB, 3 RB, 4 WR, 2 TE, 3 flex (RB/WR/TE), 2 superflex (QB/RB/WR/TE), 1 DST and 1 kicker.
meeting: Items for discussion: the prize structure, and anything else.
Put a suggestion to the commissioner or on the WhatsApp group.
draft_prep: Make sure there is room in your roster and taxi squad for your picks.
The taxi squad must be emptied of second-year players.
roster_deadline: Any roster over the limit will have players cut. Which players is the commissioner's to decide.
post_season: The league is renewed on Sleeper. Its history and records are kept forever.
The bench goes up to 23. The taxi squad stays as it is.
No free agency and no waivers in the post-season.
A player dropped now is not recoverable: he goes into the pool for August's free agency auction, and to waivers after that.
Trading reopens, and the rookie draft order is set.
